Market Domination host Josh Lipton and Yahoo Finance senior reporter Allie Canal track several of the day's top trending stock tickers, including Netflix (NFLX) facing share pressures this week after Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk called for a boycott over the platform's children's content; HSBC securities and Mizuho analysts both upgrading Occidental Petroleum (OXY) amid Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK-A, BRK-B) deal to acquire OxyChem for $9.7 billion; and shares of dating app Bumble (BMBL) receiving a downgrade.

content.title: Berkshire Hathaway preps CEO change, Cracker Barrel dumps ad firm
content.description:
Yahoo Finance's John Hyland tracks today's top moving stocks and biggest market stories in this Market Minute.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B, BRK-A) voted to separate its chairman and CEO roles, allowing Greg Abel to succeed Buffett as CEO next year.

Applied Materials (AMAT) stock is under pressure after the company noted it expects to incur a $600 million loss from Chinese sales restrictions.

Cracker Barrel (CBRL) has officially ended its professional relationship with the marketing firm behind its controversial and brief logo change.

Stay up to date on the latest market action, minute-by-minute, with Yahoo Finance's Market Minute.

content.title: Buffett Scores Win in Berkshire’s Deal for Occidental Chemicals Unit
content.summary: Score one for Warren Buffett at the expense of  Occidental Petroleum  CEO Vicki Hollub.  It looks like Buffett’s  Berkshire Hathaway  got the better of Occidental Petroleum in its purchase of the energy company’s chemical business for $9.7 billion in cash, announced earlier Thursday.  Occidental shares fell 7.1% to $44.32, against a 1% drop in the  exchange-traded fund.
